items.title: US stocks today: US stocks end higher as healthcare stocks lift Dow, tech a breather
items.summary: Wall Street ended higher on Tuesday, led by the Dow as investors shifted towards healthcare and other value stocks. The S&P 500 also gained, while the Nasdaq slipped as technology stocks paused after a rebound in the previous session. Healthcare shares gained, while small-caps and defensive sectors also outperformed.

items.title: Copper stays range bound as US tariff uncertainty, oil inflation risks weigh
items.summary: Copper prices remained range bound as uncertainty over potential US tariffs and inflation risks from higher oil prices kept traders cautious. China’s copper scrap shortage supported refined copper demand, while record high US inventories and cautious buying limited gains. Goldman Sachs expects copper prices to average $15,400 a ton in 2027.

items.title: In second visit within months, Rubio calls on India to scale up US energy and defence buys
items.summary: India and the US are actively working to expand energy and defence cooperation amidst existing tensions. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized India's potential as a crude oil refining superpower. Discussions included increasing energy trade and promoting the purchase of American technologies for mutual benefit. Rubio also plans to visit Reliance Industries Ltd's Jamnagar Refinery to discuss energy security.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday

items.title: Aerospace and military contractors raise 2026 profit forecasts
items.summary: Northrop Grumman and RTX have raised their annual profit forecasts due to strong military demand. The companies reported record backlogs of $109.6 billion and $340 billion respectively. Sustained commercial aerospace services demand has also contributed to their growth. GE Aerospace, while performing well, has warned about potential declines in demand due to high fuel prices.
